mechanism_narrative: The continued fall in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last four weeks suppresses discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week mean over the next month. The effect is strongest when both series keep making week-on-week declines.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stabilize or rise for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC still keeps falling over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RESIDENTIAL time indicates more out-of-home activity and lower at-home substitution, which should raise RETAIL_REC within the next one to two weeks. The signal fails if RESIDENTIAL does not decline further from its current elevated level.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +6.0 and then turns down week-on-week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays at or above its current level for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS decline less than WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, outdoor substitution weakens and more trips are reallocated to indoor retail, supporting higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires PARKS to stop falling first.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stops declining while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -30
failure_condition: If PARKS continue to fall at least as fast as WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, yet RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A deepening contraction in TRANSIT below its current trough signals broader access constraints and weaker shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next month. The prediction is violated if transit recovery starts first.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50 and remains there for two weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains above -50 or rebounds while RETAIL_REC still drops, this threshold mechanism is not supported.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized easing in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT should increase daytime circulation and spill over into retail visits within one week, producing a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks. The effect is stronger when both series rise together rather than separately.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued fall in PARKS during a normal weekly cycle indicates shifting activity away from outdoor recreation and toward indoor shopping, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The signal fails if park usage rebounds instead of continuing its seasonal decline.
failure_condition: If PARKS rise over the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC still improves, the seasonal substitution story is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM falls while RESIDENTIAL rises, households are consolidating errands and spending less time on retail trips, which pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism depends on the two series moving in opposite directions.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -25 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near current levels and RESIDENTIAL does not remain elevated, yet RETAIL_REC still falls, this interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening regime, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate reduced mobility compliance and broader access restrictions, which will keep RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week average over the next month. If either series reverses, the effect weakens materially.
failure_condition: If tightening conditions persist but TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rebound for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC does not fall, the hypothesis fails.
